title: LeakLens audit report (report-1)
description: The JSON document written by a LeakLens audit when --json is passed. This version is frozen: a change that removes or retypes a field needs a new report-2 schema, while a command that adds its own section (dl, pipeline, clustering) is additive and stays valid here.

$schema.description: The schema this document claims to follow. Absent on documents written before report-1 was published.

schema.description: Format identifier, matching the schema name for surfaces that carry a version too (baselines use schema plus version).

trust_score.description: 0-100 health of the audited dataset or code, higher is better. Computed from the findings that survived policy (baseline, suppressions).

counts.description: Findings by severity, over every finding, suppressed ones included. Present on the text, dl and image reports; the data audit leaves the tally to the consumer.

findings.description: Every finding the detectors produced, including suppressed ones, in detector order.

policy.description: What the baseline and suppressions did. Empty when neither is configured.

diagnostics.description: Suppression rules that were refused, and why.

resolved.description: Baseline entries this audit no longer produces. Omitted when no baseline was compared.

field.description: Document field that was audited for text datasets, otherwise null.

documents.description: Rows or documents read per split.

skipped.description: Rows or documents a reader could not use, per split.

counts.description: Findings by severity, over every finding, suppressed ones included.

fingerprint.description: Versioned SHA-256 identity of the logical finding, stable across runs and line moves.

evidence.description: One reason a detector fired. Optional fields are omitted when absent, never null.

source.description: Where the evidence came from, such as data, code or artifact.

kind.description: The evidence class, such as statistic, column, row or span.
Detector that produced the finding, such as target_leakage or split_overlap.

diagnostic.description: Present and true only on findings that describe the audit itself rather than the data.

status.description: Present when a baseline or suppression rule applied to this finding.

suppression.description: The rule that suppressed the finding.
